mainEvent.title: Wed 11/25 · PCE inflation, Q3 GDP, durable goods and jobless claims all land at 8:30a
mainEvent.body: Thanksgiving squeezes the week's data into Wednesday morning. October core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is expected to rise **0.3%** on the month and **3.2%** on the year, up from 3.1%, with headline PCE seen at 3.8% from 3.6% (AskTraders, FXEmpire, Newsquawk); Polymarket puts exactly 3.2% at about 58%. The second estimate of Q3 GDP (advance **3.4%**), October durable goods and jobless claims, moved up a day, come out at the same time, then new home sales at 10:00a and the Fed's Beige Book at 2:00p. A December 9 hike is almost fully priced after last week's hawkish minutes, so a hot print could revive talk of a half-point move, while a soft one would back Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday warning against over-tightening. Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 on Tuesday, well above the 92 expected, and Dell beat by a wide margin after the close. Markets are shut Thursday and close at 1:00p Friday.

stories.title: Chips give back part of Monday's surge as the Dow closes above 50,000 for the first time.
stories.body: A day after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang and stocks had their best day since April 2025, chipmakers reversed: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell **7.9%** with all 30 members lower (Options Oracle, TradingKey). Nvidia fell **5.9%** to about $155.38, after Monday's 31.5% jump to $165.05; Micron lost 11%, AMD 8.9%, Intel 8.2% and Broadcom 4% (StockTitan, Investing.com). The S&P 500 slipped **0.50%** to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq **1.48%** to 23,733.54, while the Dow rose 423.39 points (0.85%) to **50,018.70**, its first close above 50,000, helped by Amgen, Nike and Salesforce, and the Russell 2000 gained 0.57% to 2,684.94 (Vista Partners, Sell The News, ad-hoc-news). Health care (XLV) rose 3.0% and staples 1.7%, while tech (XLK) fell 3.3%. Goldman's positioning gauge is at the 36th percentile, the lowest since Liberation Day (24/7 Wall St.). Nvidia's board said it got "input from senior levels of the United States government" before reinstating Huang, and its independent committee looking into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion" (Nvidia release, SEC 8-K). Still open: the SEC accounting review reported Friday, and the 10-Q due Dec 4 (FourWeekMBA). Polymarket's odds of Nvidia ending 2026 above $4T with Huang as CEO fell to about 36% from 50% on Monday.

stories.title: Dell crushes estimates and raises its outlook after the close; HP jumps, Workday and Nutanix slip.
stories.body: Dell earned **$9.45** a share adjusted vs about $6.56–6.63 expected on revenue of **$54.94B** vs $49.2–50.6B, guided Q4 revenue to $56.3B vs about $53.6B and EPS to $8.40 vs about $7.50, and raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $29.68 from $25.50 and revenue to $202B from $192B; its AI server backlog is $132.3B and it added a $25B buyback (Investing.com, FinanceFeeds). The stock had fallen 11.8% to $295.28 in the regular session and was up about 2–4% after hours. HP Inc. earned $0.83 vs $0.75 on revenue of $16.0B vs $15.4B, guided fiscal 2027 EPS to $3.15–3.45 vs $3.18 expected and rose about 9% after hours. Workday beat ($2.82 vs $2.75; revenue $2.71B vs $2.69B) but its Q4 subscription guide of $2.60B was a touch below $2.61B, and it fell about 4%. Autodesk beat ($3.20 vs $3.07) and Nutanix beat ($0.73 vs $0.61) but its full-year revenue guide midpoint was below estimates; they fell about 4% and 9%. Urban Outfitters earned $1.54 vs $1.52 on in-line sales and fell about 11% (after-hours moves from Investing.com at 4:25p). Deere reports Wednesday before the open.

stories.title: Retailers and health care lead: Abercrombie and Kohl's jump about 20%, Insmed gets a $41B bid, Analog Devices sinks 17%.
stories.body: Abercrombie rose **19.7%** after record Q3 sales of about $1.4B beat estimates, and Kohl's **19.5%** as one-time gains lifted its profit outlook to $4.30–4.50 a share vs $2.14 expected (StockTitan, Investing.com, Seeking Alpha). Dick's gained 14.6% after earning $1.94 adjusted vs about $1.40 and raising its 2026 outlook to $11.45–12.30; Dollar Tree rose 11.2% after comps of 4.6% and a higher full-year outlook of $8.05–8.25; Burlington rose 3.9% despite cutting its Q4 outlook by $0.20 on fuel and freight; and Best Buy 2.7% after earning $1.62 vs $1.49 with comps up 6.1% (company releases, SEC 8-Ks, StockTitan). Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for **$175 a share** in cash, about $41B; Insmed rose 14% to about $170 and Sanofi's US shares 11% (Sanofi release, Vista Partners, StockTitan). Health care (XLV) gained 3.0%, the best sector. On the other side, Analog Devices fell **17.4%** after guiding Q1 EPS to $3.82 ± $0.20 vs $3.86 expected despite revenue of $4.37B vs $4.32B, and HPE fell 16.3% despite Monday's beat and guide raise (StockTitan, Investing.com). Medtronic slipped more than 3% before the open after revenue of $9.36B missed $9.48B (Reuters).

stories.title: Consumer confidence jumps to a near two-year high as markets lock in a December hike before PCE.
stories.body: The Conference Board's index rose to **103.3** in November from a revised 91.9, above every estimate in Bloomberg's survey (consensus about 92) and the highest since January 2025. The present-situation index climbed 13.7 points to 132.8 and expectations 9.9 points to 83.6; 30.8% said jobs were plentiful, up from 26.2%, the most since May 2025 (Conference Board via StockAnalysis, Reuters via rallies.ai). Senior economist Fergus McCormick tied the gain to "lower uncertainty following the midterm elections," while consumers "continued to express frustration with high prices." CME FedWatch has about 95% on a 25bp hike on December 9 and 5% on 50bp (Yahoo Finance); Kalshi has 25bp at **92%**, a hold at 5% and a bigger hike at 3% (Tue 11/24 close). On Monday NY Fed President Williams said there is "still work to do" on inflation, seeing it at 3.5% at the end of 2026 and 2% in 2028 (Reuters). The 10Y ended about 4.90%, down 1bp. Next: core PCE Wednesday at 8:30a (est 3.2% y/y; Polymarket about 58% on exactly 3.2%), Q3 GDP, durable goods and claims at the same time, and the Beige Book at 2:00p; the pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

stories.title: Anthropic closes below its $83 IPO price.
stories.body: Anthropic (**ANT**) fell about **6.5%** to $81.91, its first close below the $83 IPO price and a third straight drop (Investing.com, Vista Partners). Needham pointed to the company's capital needs, a possible insider-selling overhang and post-IPO profit-taking (Yahoo Finance). It slipped 1.4% Monday even as Nvidia jumped 31%, and is now about 16% below its $97.17 debut close and 27% below the $111.50 opening trade on Thursday (FinanceFeeds, TipRanks). The deal raised about $93.5B including selling holders, plus a $26B private placement at $83 with Microsoft, Google, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom (TipRanks). Its fade from the opening print was one of the triggers of last week's AI selloff (AP, Reuters).

stories.title: Oil bounces off a three-month low as ships are hit near Hormuz.
stories.body: January WTI ended the session about **$81.5**, up about 1.6%, after touching $79.07 intraday, its weakest since Aug 10, and Brent dipped as low as $88.10, its lowest since Aug 27 (Vista Partners, Reuters via MarineLink); final settlements couldn't be confirmed. Three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles while sailing east through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with all crews accounted for (UKMTO), and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a container ship was targeted; Al Jazeera puts Hormuz oil traffic down about 40%. "Expectations for excess supply continue to restrain the recovery": Deutsche Bank says October inventories imply an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels a day, Libya's Sharara pipeline has reopened, and China and India are on track for record Russian imports (Reuters via MarineLink, rallies.ai). On Monday Brent settled at $89.37 and January WTI at $80.17, three-month lows (Reuters via OK Energy Today). OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output.
